question: For white-on-red signs, what minimum maintained retroreflectivity values and contrast criterion are shown in Table 2A-5?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 2A-5 shows that white-on-red signs must maintain a minimum retroreflectivity of W ≥ 35 for the white element and R ≥ 7 for the red element (in cd/lx/m², measured at a 0.2° observation angle and a -4.0° entrance angle); these values apply across all sheeting types in the table. In addition, footnote 4 imposes a minimum sign contrast ratio of ≥ 3:1, calculated as white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity. Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." Guidance (recommended): - Except for signs identified in Paragraph 5, one or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), FHWA, or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5; signs identified as being below the minimum levels should be replaced. Options (permitted): - Table 2A-5 lists "White on Red — W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7" applicable across the beaded (Types I, II, III) and prismatic sheeting columns. - Footnote 4 to the table states: "Minimum sign contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity)." - Footnote 1 states the values "are in units of cd/lx/m² measured at an observation angle of 0.2° and an entrance angle of -4.0°." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows the White on Red row of Table 2A-5 with "W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7" spanning all sheeting-type columns and referencing footnote 4, which specifies the ≥ 3:1 white-to-red contrast ratio; [Image 2] (Page 103) shows the surrounding Section 2A.22 provisions requiring maintenance at or above the Table 2A-5 levels; [Image 3] (Page 104) shows the full Table 2A-5 including the White on Red row and footnotes 1 and 4. Citations: - Table 2A-5 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Option §3 (p.63) - Section 2A.22 Option §4 (p.63) - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62)
gold_answer: White at least 35 cd/lx/m², red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and a white-to-red contrast ratio of at least 3:1.
